Let us denote by $\left(\mathcal{V},\|\|\right)$ any normed vector space.

#### Lemma A.

For any $f:\mathcal{V}\times\mathcal{V}\to\mathbb{R},g:\mathcal{V}\times\mathcal{V}\to\mathbb{R}$ , we have that:

$$ \displaystyle\left\|\underset{a\in\mathcal{V}}{\sup}\>f(a)-\underset{a\in\mathcal{V}}{\sup}\>g(a)\right\|\leq\underset{a\in\mathcal{V}}{\sup}\>\left\|f(a)-g(a)\right\|. $$

#### Proof.

$$ \displaystyle f(a) \displaystyle\leq\left\|f(a)-g(a)\right\|+g(a) \displaystyle\implies\underset{a\in\mathcal{V}}{\sup}f(a) \displaystyle\leq\underset{a\in\mathcal{V}}{\sup}\{\left\|f(a)-g(a)\right\|+g(a)\} \displaystyle\leq\underset{a\in\mathcal{V}}{\sup}\left\|f(a)-g(a)\right\|+\underset{a\in\mathcal{V}}{\sup}\;g(a). $$

Deducting $\underset{a\in\mathcal{V}}{\sup}\;g(a)$ from both sides of (20) yields:

$$ \displaystyle\underset{a\in\mathcal{V}}{\sup}f(a)-\underset{a\in\mathcal{V}}{\sup}g(a)\leq\underset{a\in\mathcal{V}}{\sup}\left\|f(a)-g(a)\right\|. $$

After reversing the roles of $f$ and $g$ and redoing steps (19) - (20), we deduce the desired result since the RHS of (21) is unchanged. ∎

The proof of the Theorem 1 is established through the following results:

#### Lemma B.

For any c-SPG, the state transitivity conditions holds whenever the reward functions takes the following form:

$$ \displaystyle R_{i}(s,(a^{i},a^{-i}))=g(s,(a^{i},a^{-i}))+k(s)h_{i}(a^{i},a^{-i}), $$

for any functions $g,k,h$ for which $k^{-1}$ exists.

#### Proof.

To prove the result, we show that the class of games can be rescaled accordingly. Indeed, we first note that $k^{-1}(s)R_{i}(s,(a^{i},a^{-i}))-k^{-1}(s^{\prime})R_{i}(s^{\prime},(a^{i},a^{-i}))=k^{-1}(s)g(s,(a^{i},a^{-i}))-k^{-1}(s^{\prime})g(s^{\prime},(a^{i},a^{-i}))$ . Using the invertibility of $k$ , we now consider a rescaled game $\mathcal{M}(s)=\langle\left(\mathcal{A}_{i}\right)_{i\in\mathcal{N}},\left(V_{i}(s)\right)_{i\in\mathcal{N}},\mathcal{N}\rangle$ where $V_{i}:=k^{-1}R_{i}$ , then it is easy to see that for these games we have: $V_{i}(s,(a^{i},a^{-i}))-V_{i}(s^{\prime},(a^{i},a^{-i}))=L(s,(a^{i},a^{-i}))-L(s^{\prime},(a^{i},a^{-i}))$ where $L:=k^{-1}g$ and hence the state transitivity assumption is satisfied. ∎

#### Lemma C.

For any PG, there exists a function $B:\boldsymbol{\Pi}\times\mathcal{S}\to\mathbb{R}$ ( $B\in\mathcal{H}$ ) such that the following holds for any $i\in\mathcal{N},\forall(a^{i}_{t},a^{-i}_{t})\in\boldsymbol{\mathcal{A}},\forall s\in\mathcal{S}$ $R_{i}(s,a^{i}_{t},a^{-i}_{t})=\phi(s,a^{i}_{t},a^{-i}_{t})+F_{i}(s,a^{-i}_{t})$ where $F_{i}$ satisfies $F_{i}(s,a^{-i}_{t})=F_{i}(s^{\prime},a^{-i}_{t})$ .

The result generalises dummy-coordination separability known in PGs to a state-based setting (Slade, 1994; Ui, 2000).

#### Proof of Lemma C.

To establish the forward implication, we make the following observation which is straightforward:

$$ \displaystyle R_{i}(s,a^{i}_{t},a^{-i}_{t})-R_{i}(s,a^{\prime i}_{t},a^{-i}_{t}) \displaystyle=\phi(s,a^{i}_{t},a^{-i}_{t})+F_{i}(s,a^{-i}_{t})-\left(\phi(s,a^{i}_{t},a^{-i}_{t})+F_{i}(s,a^{-i}_{t})\right) \displaystyle=\phi(s,a^{i}_{t},a^{-i}_{t})-\phi(s,a^{i}_{t},a^{-i}_{t}) $$

To prove the reverse assume that the game is a state-based potential game. Let us now define the function $T_{i}(s,a^{i}_{t},a^{-i}_{t}):=R_{i}(s,a^{i}_{t},a^{-i}_{t})-\phi(s,a^{i}_{t},a^{-i}_{t})$ , then we observe that: $R_{i}(s,a^{i}_{t},a^{-i}_{t})-R_{i}(s,a^{\prime i}_{t},a^{-i}_{t})=\phi(s,a^{i}_{t},a^{-i}_{t})-\phi(s,a^{\prime i}_{t},a^{-i}_{t})\iff R_{i}(s,a^{i}_{t},a^{-i}_{t})-\phi(s,a^{i}_{t},a^{-i}_{t})=R_{i}(s,a^{\prime i}_{t},a^{-i}_{t})-\phi(s,a^{\prime i}_{t},a^{-i}_{t})$ and hence $T_{i}(s,a^{i}_{t},a^{-i}_{t})=T_{i}(s,a^{\prime i}_{t},a^{-i}_{t})$ which implies that $T_{i}(s,a^{i}_{t},a^{-i}_{t})\equiv K_{i}(s,a^{-i}_{t})$ . In a similar way, writing $T_{i}(s,a^{i}_{t},a^{-i}_{t}):=R_{i}(s,a^{i}_{t},a^{-i}_{t})-\phi(s,a^{i}_{t},a^{-i}_{t})$ and using the state transitive property, we deduce that $T_{i}(s^{\prime},a^{i}_{t},a^{-i}_{t})=T_{i}(s,a^{i}_{t},a^{-i}_{t})$ which settles the proof. ∎

### H.2 Proof of Main Results

### Proof of Theorem 1

#### Proposition 4.

There exists a function $B:\boldsymbol{\Pi}\times\mathcal{S}\to\mathbb{R}$ ( $B\in\mathcal{H}$ ) and the following holds for any $i\in\mathcal{N}$

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{s\sim P(\cdot|)}\left[v^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}_{i}(s)-v^{\boldsymbol{\pi^{\prime}}}_{i}(s)\right]=\mathbb{E}_{s\sim P(\cdot|)}\left[B^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}(s)-B^{\boldsymbol{\pi^{\prime}}}(s)\right]. $$

#### Proof.

We prove the proposition in two parts beginning with the finite case then extending to the infinite horizon case.

Hence, we first seek to show that for any joint strategy $(\pi_{i},\pi_{-i})\in\boldsymbol{\Pi}$ , define by $v_{i,k}$ the value function for the finite horizon game of length $k\in\mathbb{N}$ (i.e. $v^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}_{i,k}(s):=\mathbb{E}_{s_{t}\sim P,\pi_{i},\pi_{-i}}\left[\sum_{t=0}^{k}\gamma^{t}R_{i}(s_{t},\boldsymbol{a}_{t})|s\equiv s_{0}\right]$ for any $i\in\mathcal{N}$ and $k<\infty$ ). Then there exists a function $B_{k}:\boldsymbol{\Pi}\times\mathcal{S}\to\mathbb{R}$ such that the following holds for any $i\in\mathcal{N}$ and $\forall\pi_{i},\pi^{\prime}_{i}\in\Pi_{i},\forall\pi_{-i}\in\Pi_{-i}$ :

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{s\sim P(\cdot|)}\left[v^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}_{i,k}(s)-v^{\boldsymbol{\pi^{\prime}}}_{i,k}(s)\right]=\mathbb{E}_{s\sim P(\cdot|)}\left[B_{k}^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}(s)-B_{k}^{\boldsymbol{\pi^{\prime}}}(s)\right]. $$

For the finite horizon case, the result is proven by induction on the number of time steps until the end of the game. Unlike the infinite horizon case, for the finite horizon case the value function and policy have an explicit time dependence.

We consider the case of the proposition at time $T-1$ that is we evaluate the value functions at the penultimate time step. In the following, we employ the shorthands $\boldsymbol{a}_{k}\equiv(a^{i}_{k},a^{-i}_{k})$ and by $\boldsymbol{a^{\prime}}_{k}\equiv(a^{{}^{\prime}i}_{k},a^{-i}_{k})$ for any $k\in\mathbb{N}$ and similarly $\boldsymbol{\pi}(\cdot)\equiv\prod_{j\in\mathcal{N}}\pi_{j}$ and $\boldsymbol{\pi^{\prime}}(\cdot)\equiv\prod_{j\in\mathcal{N}/\{i\}}\pi_{j}(\cdot)\cdot\pi^{\prime}_{i}(\cdot)$ . We will also use the shorthands $F^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}\equiv F^{(\pi_{i},\pi_{-i})}$ and $F^{\boldsymbol{\pi^{\prime}}}\equiv F^{(\pi^{\prime}_{i},\pi_{-i})}$ given some function $F$ .

In what follows and for the remainder of the script, we employ the following shorthands:

$$ \displaystyle\mathcal{P}^{\boldsymbol{a}}_{ss^{\prime}}=:P(s^{\prime};\boldsymbol{a},s),\quad\mathcal{P}^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}_{ss^{\prime}}=:\int_{\boldsymbol{\mathcal{A}}}d\boldsymbol{a}_{t}\boldsymbol{\pi}(\boldsymbol{a}_{t}|s)\mathcal{P}^{\boldsymbol{a}_{t}}_{ss^{\prime}},\quad\mathcal{R}_{i}^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}(s_{t}):=\int_{\boldsymbol{\mathcal{A}}}d\boldsymbol{a}_{t}\boldsymbol{\pi}(\boldsymbol{a}_{t}|s_{t})R_{i}(s_{t},\boldsymbol{a}_{t}) \displaystyle\boldsymbol{\phi}^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}(s_{t}):=\int_{\boldsymbol{\mathcal{A}}}d\boldsymbol{a}_{t}\boldsymbol{\pi}(\boldsymbol{a}_{t}|s_{t})\phi(s_{t},\boldsymbol{a}_{t}),\quad\boldsymbol{F}_{i}^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}(s_{t}):=\int_{\boldsymbol{\mathcal{A}}}d\boldsymbol{a}_{t}\boldsymbol{\pi}(\boldsymbol{a}_{t}|s_{t})F_{i}(s_{t},\boldsymbol{a}_{t}),\quad\boldsymbol{v}_{i,k}^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}(s_{t}):=\int_{\boldsymbol{\mathcal{A}}}d\boldsymbol{a}_{t}\boldsymbol{\pi}(\boldsymbol{a}_{t}|s_{t})v^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}_{i,k}(s_{t},\boldsymbol{a}_{t}) $$

In this case, we have that:

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{s_{T-1}\sim P(\cdot|)}\left[v^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}_{i,T-1}(s_{T-1})-v^{\boldsymbol{\pi^{\prime}}}_{i,T-1}(s_{T-1})\right] \displaystyle=\mathbb{E}_{s_{T-1}\sim P(\cdot|)}\left[\mathcal{R}_{i}^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}(s_{T})+\gamma\int_{\mathcal{S}}ds_{T}\int_{\boldsymbol{\mathcal{A}}}\mathcal{P}^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}_{s_{T}s_{T-1}}v_{i}^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}(s_{T})-\left(\mathcal{R}_{i}^{\boldsymbol{\pi^{\prime}}}(s_{T})+\gamma\int_{\mathcal{S}}ds_{T}\mathcal{P}^{\boldsymbol{\pi^{\prime}}}_{s_{T}s_{T-1}}v_{i}^{\boldsymbol{\pi^{\prime}}}(s_{T})\right)\right] \displaystyle=\mathbb{E}_{s_{T-1}\sim P(\cdot|)}\Bigg[\boldsymbol{\phi}^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}(s_{T})-\boldsymbol{\phi}^{\boldsymbol{\pi^{\prime}}}(s_{T})+\gamma\int_{\mathcal{S}}ds_{T}\mathcal{P}^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}_{s_{T}s_{T-1}}v_{i}^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}(s_{T})-\gamma\int_{\mathcal{S}}ds\mathcal{P}^{\boldsymbol{\pi^{\prime}}}_{s_{T}s_{T-1}}v_{i}^{\boldsymbol{\pi^{\prime}}}(s_{T})\Bigg] \displaystyle\begin{aligned} =\mathbb{E}_{s_{T-1}\sim P(\cdot|)}\Bigg[&\boldsymbol{\phi}^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}(s_{T-1})-\boldsymbol{\phi}^{\boldsymbol{\pi^{\prime}}}(s_{T-1})+\gamma\mathbb{E}_{s_{T}\sim P(\cdot|)}\Bigg[\boldsymbol{v}_{i}^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}(s_{T})-\boldsymbol{v}_{i}^{\boldsymbol{\pi^{\prime}}}(s_{T})\Bigg]\Bigg].\end{aligned} $$

We now observe that for any $\pi_{i}\in\Pi_{i}$ and for any $\pi_{-i}\in\Pi_{-i}$ we have that $\forall i\in\mathcal{N},\;v_{i}^{\pi^{i},\pi^{-i}}(s_{T})=\mathbb{E}_{s_{T}\sim P(\cdot|)}\left[\mathcal{R}_{i}^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}(s_{T})\right]$ , moreover we have that for any $\pi_{i},\pi_{i}^{\prime}\in\Pi_{i}$ and for any $i\in\mathcal{N}$ , we have

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{s_{T}\sim P(\cdot|)}\Bigg[\mathcal{R}_{i}^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}(s_{T})-\mathcal{R}_{i}^{\boldsymbol{\pi^{\prime}}}(s_{T})\Bigg] \displaystyle=\int_{\mathcal{S}}ds_{T}\mathcal{P}^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}_{s_{T}s_{T-1}}\mathcal{R}_{i}^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}(s_{T})-\int_{\mathcal{S}}ds_{T}\mathcal{P}^{\boldsymbol{\pi^{\prime}}}_{s_{T}s_{T-1}}\mathcal{R}_{i}^{\boldsymbol{\pi^{\prime}}}(s_{T}) \displaystyle=\int_{\mathcal{S}}ds_{T}\mathcal{P}^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}_{s_{T}s_{T-1}}\left[\boldsymbol{\phi}^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}(s_{T})+\boldsymbol{F}_{i}(a^{-i}_{T})\right]-\int_{\mathcal{S}}ds_{T}\mathcal{P}^{\boldsymbol{\pi^{\prime}}}_{s_{T}s_{T-1}}\left[\boldsymbol{\phi}^{\boldsymbol{\pi^{\prime}}}(s_{T})+\boldsymbol{F}_{i}(a^{-i}_{T})\right] \displaystyle=\int_{\mathcal{S}}ds_{T}\mathcal{P}^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}_{s_{T}s_{T-1}}\boldsymbol{\phi}^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}(s_{T})-\int_{\mathcal{S}}ds_{T}\mathcal{P}^{\boldsymbol{\pi^{\prime}}}_{s_{T}s_{T-1}}\boldsymbol{\phi}^{\boldsymbol{\pi^{\prime}}}(s_{T})+\int_{\mathcal{S}}ds_{T}\mathcal{P}^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}_{s_{T}s_{T-1}}\boldsymbol{F}_{i}(a^{-i}_{T})-\int_{\mathcal{S}}ds_{T}\mathcal{P}^{\boldsymbol{\pi^{\prime}}}_{s_{T}s_{T-1}}\boldsymbol{F}_{i}(a^{-i}_{T}) \displaystyle=\int_{\mathcal{S}}ds_{T}\mathcal{P}^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}_{s_{T}s_{T-1}}\boldsymbol{\phi}^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}(s_{T})-\int_{\mathcal{S}}ds_{T}\mathcal{P}^{\boldsymbol{\pi^{\prime}}}_{s_{T}s_{T-1}}\boldsymbol{\phi}^{\boldsymbol{\pi^{\prime}}}(s_{T}) \displaystyle=\mathbb{E}_{s_{T}\sim P(\cdot|)}\left[\boldsymbol{\phi}^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}(s_{T})-\boldsymbol{\phi}^{\boldsymbol{\pi^{\prime}}}(s_{T})\right] $$

Since

$$ \displaystyle\int_{\mathcal{S}}ds_{T}\mathcal{P}^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}_{s_{T}s_{T-1}}\boldsymbol{F}_{i}(a^{-i}_{T})-\int_{\mathcal{S}}ds_{T}\mathcal{P}^{\boldsymbol{\pi^{\prime}}}_{s_{T}s_{T-1}}\boldsymbol{F}_{i}(a^{-i}_{T}) \displaystyle=\int_{\mathcal{A}_{-i}}\pi_{i}(da^{i},s_{T-1})F_{i}(a^{-i})\int_{\mathcal{A}_{i}}\pi_{-i}(da^{-i},s_{T-1})\int_{\mathcal{S}}ds_{T}P(s_{T};s_{T-1},\boldsymbol{a}_{T}) \displaystyle\qquad\qquad\qquad-\int_{\mathcal{A}_{-i}}\pi^{\prime}_{i}(da^{\prime i},s_{T-1})F_{i}(a^{-i})\int_{\mathcal{A}_{i}}\pi_{-i}(da^{-i},s_{T-1})\int_{\mathcal{S}}ds_{T}P(s_{T};s_{T-1},\boldsymbol{a^{\prime}}_{T}) \displaystyle=\int_{\mathcal{A}_{-i}}\pi_{-i}(da^{-i},s_{T-1})F_{i}(a^{-i})\left\{\int_{\mathcal{A}_{i}}\pi_{i}(da^{i},s_{T-1})-\int_{\mathcal{A}_{i}}\pi^{\prime}_{i}(da^{\prime i},s_{T-1})\right\} \displaystyle=0 $$

Hence, we find that

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{s_{T-1}\sim P(\cdot|)}\left[v^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}_{i,T-1}(s_{T-1})-v^{\boldsymbol{\pi^{\prime}}}_{i,T-1}(s_{T-1})\right] \displaystyle=\mathbb{E}_{s_{T-1}\sim P(\cdot|)}\left[\boldsymbol{\phi}^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}(s_{T-1})-\boldsymbol{\phi}^{\boldsymbol{\pi^{\prime}}}(s_{T-1})+\gamma\int_{\mathcal{S}}ds_{T}\mathcal{P}^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}_{s_{T}s_{T-1}}\boldsymbol{\phi}^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}(s_{T})-\gamma\int_{\mathcal{S}}ds_{T}\mathcal{P}^{\boldsymbol{\pi^{\prime}}}_{s_{T}s_{T-1}}\boldsymbol{\phi}^{\boldsymbol{\pi^{\prime}}}(s_{T})\right] \displaystyle=\mathbb{E}_{s_{T-1}\sim P(\cdot|)}\left[\boldsymbol{\phi}^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}(s_{T-1})-\boldsymbol{\phi}^{\boldsymbol{\pi^{\prime}}}(s_{T})+\gamma\mathbb{E}_{s_{T}\sim P(s_{T}|\cdot)}\left[\boldsymbol{\phi}^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}(s_{T-1})-\boldsymbol{\phi}^{\boldsymbol{\pi^{\prime}}}(s_{T})\right]\right] \displaystyle=\mathbb{E}_{s_{T-1}\sim P(\cdot|)}\Bigg[B_{T-1}^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}(s_{T-1})-B_{T-1}^{\boldsymbol{\pi^{\prime}}}(s_{T-1})\Bigg], $$

using the iterated law of expectations in the last line and where

$$ \displaystyle B^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}_{T}(s):=\mathbb{E}_{s_{t}\sim P,\pi_{i},\pi_{-i}}\left[\sum_{t=0}^{T}\gamma^{t}\phi(s_{t},\boldsymbol{a}_{t})|s\equiv s_{0}]\right]. $$

Hence, we have succeeded in proving that the expression (22) holds for $T-k$ when $k=1$ .

Our next goal is to prove that the expression holds for any $0<k\leq T$ .

Note that for any $T\geq k>0$ , we can write (24) as

$$ \displaystyle B^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}_{T-k}(s)=\mathbb{E}_{\pi_{i},\pi_{-i}}\left[\phi(s,\boldsymbol{a}_{k})+\gamma\int_{\mathcal{S}}ds^{\prime}P(s^{\prime};s,\boldsymbol{a}_{k})B_{T-(k+1)}^{\pi^{i},\pi^{-i}}(s^{\prime})\cdot 1_{k\leq T}\right]. $$

Now we consider the case when we evaluate the expression (22) for any $0<k\leq T$ . Our inductive hypothesis is the expression holds for some $0<k\leq T$ , that is for a $0<k\leq T$ we have that:

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{s_{T-k}\sim P(\cdot|)}\left[v^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}_{i,k}(s_{T-k})-v^{\boldsymbol{\pi^{\prime}}}_{i,k}(s_{T-k})\right]=\mathbb{E}_{s_{T-k}\sim P(\cdot|)}\left[B^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}_{k}(s_{T-k})-B^{\boldsymbol{\pi^{\prime}}}_{k}(s_{T-k})\right]. $$

It is easy to see that given (25) and Lemma C, it must be the case that:

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{s_{T-k}\sim P(\cdot|)}\left[v^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}_{i,k}(s_{T-k})\right]=\mathbb{E}_{s_{T-k}\sim P(\cdot|)}\left[B^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}_{k}(s_{T-k})+G^{\pi_{-i}}_{i,k}(s_{T-k})\right]. $$

where $G^{\pi_{-i}}_{i,k}(s):=\mathbb{E}_{P,\pi_{-i}}\left[\sum_{t=0}^{k}\gamma^{t}F_{-i}(s,a_{t}^{-i})\right]$ .

Moreover, we recall that $F_{-i}$ satisfies the condition $F_{-i}(s,a^{-i}_{t})=F_{-i}(s^{\prime},a^{-i}_{t})$ , hence $G^{\pi_{-i}}_{i,k}(s)=G^{\pi_{-i}}_{i,k}(s^{\prime})$ so from now on we drop the dependence on $s$ and write $G^{\pi_{-i}}_{i,k}$ .

It remains to show that the expression holds for $k+1$ time steps prior to the end of the horizon. The result can be obtained using the dynamic programming principle and the base case ( $k=1$ ) result, indeed we have that

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{s_{T-(k+1)}\sim P(\cdot|)}\left[v^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}_{i,k+1}(s_{T-(k+1)})-v^{\boldsymbol{\pi^{\prime}}}_{i,k+1}(s_{T-(k+1)})\right] \displaystyle\begin{aligned} =\mathbb{E}_{s_{T-(k+1)}\sim P(\cdot|)}\Bigg[\mathcal{R}_{i}^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}(s_{T-(k+1)})&+\gamma\int_{\mathcal{S}}ds_{T-k}\mathcal{P}^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}_{s_{T-(k+1)}s_{T-k}}\boldsymbol{v}_{i,k}^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}(s_{T-k})\\
&-\mathcal{R}_{i}^{\boldsymbol{\pi^{\prime}}}(s_{T-(k+1)})-\gamma\int_{\mathcal{S}}ds_{T-k}\mathcal{P}^{\boldsymbol{\pi^{\prime}}}_{s_{T-(k+1)}s_{T-k}}\boldsymbol{v}_{i,k}^{\boldsymbol{\pi^{\prime}}}(s_{T-k})\Bigg]\end{aligned} \displaystyle=\mathbb{E}_{s_{T-(k+1)}\sim P(\cdot|)}\left[\mathcal{R}_{i}^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}(s_{T-(k+1)})-\mathcal{R}_{i}^{\boldsymbol{\pi^{\prime}}}(s_{T-(k+1)})\right] \displaystyle+\gamma\mathbb{E}_{s_{T-(k+1)}\sim P(\cdot|)}\Bigg[\int_{\mathcal{S}}ds\mathcal{P}^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}_{s_{T-(k+1)}s_{T-k}}\boldsymbol{v}_{i,k}^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}(s_{T-k})-\mathcal{P}^{\boldsymbol{\pi^{\prime}}}_{s_{T-(k+1)}s_{T-k}}\boldsymbol{v}_{i,k}^{\boldsymbol{\pi^{\prime}}}(s_{T-k})\Bigg]. $$

Studying the terms under the first expression, we observe that by construction, we have that:

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{s_{T-(k+1)}\sim P(\cdot|)}\Bigg[\mathcal{R}_{i}^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}(s_{T-(k+1)})-\mathcal{R}_{i}^{\boldsymbol{\pi^{\prime}}}(s_{T-(k+1)})\Bigg]=\mathbb{E}_{s_{T-(k+1)}\sim P(\cdot|)}\left[\boldsymbol{\phi}^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}(s_{T-(k+1)})-\boldsymbol{\phi}^{\boldsymbol{\pi}^{\prime}}(s_{T-(k+1)})\right]. $$

We now study the terms within the second expectation.

Using (25) (i.e. the inductive hypothesis), we find that:

$$ \displaystyle\int_{\mathcal{S}}ds_{T-k}\mathcal{P}^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}_{s_{T-k}s_{T-k-1}}\boldsymbol{v}_{i,k}^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}(s_{T-k})-\int_{\mathcal{S}}ds_{T-k}\mathcal{P}^{\boldsymbol{\pi^{\prime}}}_{s_{T-k}s_{T-k-1}}\boldsymbol{v}_{i,k}^{\boldsymbol{\pi^{\prime}}}(s_{T-k}) \displaystyle=\int_{\mathcal{S}}ds_{T-k}\mathcal{P}^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}_{s_{T-k}s_{T-k-1}}\left[\boldsymbol{B}_{k}^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}(s_{T-k})+\boldsymbol{G}_{i,k}^{\pi_{-i}}\right]-\int_{\mathcal{S}}ds_{T-k}\mathcal{P}^{\boldsymbol{\pi^{\prime}}}_{s_{T-k}s_{T-k-1}}\left[\boldsymbol{B}_{k}^{\boldsymbol{\pi^{\prime}}}(s_{T-k})+\boldsymbol{G}_{i,k}^{\pi_{-i}}\right] \displaystyle\begin{aligned} =\int_{\mathcal{S}}ds_{T-k}\mathcal{P}^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}_{s_{T-k}s_{T-k-1}}\boldsymbol{B}_{k}^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}(s_{T-k})&-\int_{\mathcal{S}}ds_{T-k}\mathcal{P}^{\boldsymbol{\pi^{\prime}}}_{s_{T-k}s_{T-k-1}}\boldsymbol{B}_{k}^{\boldsymbol{\pi^{\prime}}}(s_{T-k})\\
&+\int_{\mathcal{S}}ds_{T-k}\mathcal{P}^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}_{s_{T-k}s_{T-k-1}}\boldsymbol{G}_{i,k}^{\pi_{-i}}-\int_{\mathcal{S}}ds_{T-k}\mathcal{P}^{\boldsymbol{\pi^{\prime}}}_{s_{T-k}s_{T-k-1}}\boldsymbol{G}_{i,k}^{\pi_{-i}}\end{aligned} $$

We now observe that

$$ \displaystyle\int_{\mathcal{S}}ds_{T-k}\mathcal{P}^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}_{s_{T-k}s_{T-k-1}}\boldsymbol{G}_{i,k}^{\pi_{-i}}-\int_{\mathcal{S}}ds_{T-k}\mathcal{P}^{\boldsymbol{\pi^{\prime}}}_{s_{T-k}s_{T-k-1}}\boldsymbol{G}_{i,k}^{\pi_{-i}} \displaystyle=\int_{\mathcal{S}}ds_{T-k}\int_{\boldsymbol{\mathcal{A}}}\Bigg[\pi_{i}(da^{i}_{T-(k+1)},s_{T-(k+1)})-\pi^{\prime}_{i}(da^{i}_{T-(k+1)},s_{T-(k+1)})\Bigg] \displaystyle\qquad\qquad\qquad\cdot P(s_{T-k};s_{T-(k+1)},\boldsymbol{a}_{T-(k+1)})\pi_{-i}(da^{-i}_{T-(k+1)},s_{T-(k+1)})G^{\pi_{-i}}_{i,k} \displaystyle=\int_{\mathcal{S}}ds_{T-k}\int_{\mathcal{A}_{-i}}\pi_{-i}(da^{-i}_{T-(k+1)},s_{T-(k+1)}) \displaystyle\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\cdot\left(P(s_{T-k};s_{T-(k+1)},\pi_{i},a^{-i}_{T-(k+1)})-P(s_{T-k};s_{T-(k+1)},\pi^{\prime}_{i},a^{-i}_{T-(k+1)})\right)G^{\pi_{-i}}_{i,k} \displaystyle=0 $$

We now find that:

$$ \displaystyle\int_{\mathcal{S}}ds_{T-k}\mathcal{P}^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}_{s_{T-k}s_{T-k-1}}\boldsymbol{v}_{i,k}^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}(s_{T-k})-\int_{\mathcal{S}}ds_{T-k}\mathcal{P}^{\boldsymbol{\pi^{\prime}}}_{s_{T-k}s_{T-k-1}}\boldsymbol{v}_{i,k}^{\boldsymbol{\pi^{\prime}}}(s_{T-k}) \displaystyle=\int_{\mathcal{S}}ds_{T-k}\mathcal{P}^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}_{s_{T-k}s_{T-k-1}}\boldsymbol{B}_{k}^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}(s_{T-k})-\int_{\mathcal{S}}ds_{T-k}\mathcal{P}^{\boldsymbol{\pi^{\prime}}}_{s_{T-k}s_{T-k-1}}\boldsymbol{B}_{k}^{\boldsymbol{\pi^{\prime}}}(s_{T-k}) $$

Now combining (27) and (28) leads to the fact that:

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{s_{T-(k+1)}\sim P(\cdot|)}\left[v^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}_{i,k+1}(s_{T-(k+1)})-v^{\boldsymbol{\pi^{\prime}}}_{i,k+1}(s_{T-(k+1)})\right] \displaystyle\begin{aligned} =\mathbb{E}_{s_{T-(k+1)}\sim P(\cdot|)}\Bigg[\int_{\mathcal{S}}ds_{T-k}\mathcal{P}^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}_{s_{T-k}s_{T-k-1}}\boldsymbol{B}_{k}^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}(s_{T-k})&-\int_{\mathcal{S}}ds_{T-k}\mathcal{P}^{\boldsymbol{\pi^{\prime}}}_{s_{T-k}s_{T-k-1}}\boldsymbol{B}_{k}^{\boldsymbol{\pi^{\prime}}}(s_{T-k})\Bigg]\\
&+\mathbb{E}_{s_{T-(k+1)}\sim P(\cdot|)}\left[\boldsymbol{\phi}^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}(s_{T-(k+1)})-\boldsymbol{\phi}^{\boldsymbol{\pi}^{\prime}}(s_{T-(k+1)})\right]\end{aligned}, $$

from which we immediately deduce that

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{s_{T-(k+1)}\sim P(\cdot|)}\left[v^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}_{i,k+1}(s_{T-(k+1)})-v^{\boldsymbol{\pi^{\prime}}}_{i,k+1}(s_{T-(k+1)})\right]=\mathbb{E}_{s_{T-(k+1)}\sim P(\cdot|)}\left[B^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}_{k+1}(s_{T-(k+1)})-B^{\boldsymbol{\pi^{\prime}}}_{k+1}(s_{T-(k+1)})\right], $$

where

$$ \displaystyle B^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}_{k}(s)=\mathbb{E}_{\pi_{i},\pi_{-i}}\left[\phi(s_{k},\boldsymbol{a}_{k})+\gamma\int_{\mathcal{S}}ds^{\prime}P(s^{\prime};s,\boldsymbol{a}_{k})B_{k-1}^{\pi^{i},\pi^{-i}}(s^{\prime})\right], $$

from which we deduce the result. ∎

Thus far we have established the relation (23) holds only for the finite horizon case. We now extend the coverage to the infinite horizon case in which we can recover the use of stationary strategies. Before doing so, we require the following results:

#### Lemma D.

For any $t^{\prime}<\infty$ , define by $B^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}_{t^{\prime}}:\mathbb{N}\times\Pi_{i}\times\Pi_{-i}\times\mathcal{S}\to\mathbb{R}$ the following function:

$$ \displaystyle B^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}_{t^{\prime}}(s):=\mathbb{E}_{s_{t}\sim P,\pi_{i},\pi_{-i}}\left[\sum_{t=0}^{T}\gamma^{t}\phi(s_{t},\boldsymbol{a}_{t})|s\equiv s_{0}\right]. $$

then $\exists B^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}:\Pi_{i}\times\Pi_{-i}\times\mathcal{S}\to\mathbb{R}$ s.t. $\forall s\in\mathcal{S}$ and for any $\pi_{i}\in\Pi_{i},\pi_{-i}\in\Pi_{-i}$ ,

$$ \displaystyle\underset{t\to\infty}{\lim}B^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}_{t}(s)=B^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}(s), $$

where for any $\pi_{i}\in\Pi_{i},\pi_{-i}\in\Pi_{-i}$ , the function $B^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}$ is given by: $B^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}(s):=\mathbb{E}_{s_{t}\sim P,\pi_{i},\pi_{-i}}\left[\sum_{t=0}^{\infty}\gamma^{t}\phi(s_{t},\boldsymbol{a}_{t})|s\equiv s_{0}\right]$ .

#### Proof.

We prove the result by showing that the sequence $B^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}_{n},B^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}_{n+1},\ldots$ converges uniformly, that is the sequence is a Cauchy sequence. In particular, we show that $\forall\epsilon>0$ , $\exists T^{\prime}>0$ s.th. $\forall t^{\prime},t^{\prime\prime}>T^{\prime}$ and for any $\pi_{i}\in\Pi_{i},\pi_{-i}\in\Pi_{-i}$

$$ \displaystyle\left\|B^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}_{t^{\prime}}-B^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}_{t^{\prime\prime}}\right\|<\epsilon. $$

Firstly, we deduce that the function $\phi$ is bounded since each $R_{i}$ is bounded also (c.f. (43)). Now w.log., consider the case when $t^{\prime}\geq t^{\prime\prime}$ . We begin by observing the fact that

$$ \displaystyle B^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}_{t^{\prime}}(s)-B^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}_{t^{\prime\prime}}(s) \displaystyle=\mathbb{E}_{s_{t}\sim P(\cdot;s_{t-1},a_{t-1}),\pi_{i},\pi_{-i}}\left[\sum_{t=0}^{t^{\prime}}\gamma^{t}\phi_{t}(s_{t},\boldsymbol{a}_{t})-\sum_{t=0}^{t^{\prime\prime}}\gamma^{t}\phi_{t}(s_{t},\boldsymbol{a}_{t})\right] \displaystyle=\mathbb{E}_{s_{t}\sim P(\cdot;s_{t-1},a_{t-1}),\pi_{i},\pi_{-i}}\left[\sum_{t=t^{\prime\prime}}^{t^{\prime}}\gamma^{t}\phi_{t}(s_{t},\boldsymbol{a}_{t})\right]. $$

Hence, we find that

$$ \displaystyle\;\left|B^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}_{t^{\prime}}(s)-B^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}_{t^{\prime\prime}}(s)\right| \displaystyle=\left|\mathbb{E}_{s_{t}\sim P(\cdot;s_{t-1},a_{t-1}),\pi_{i},\pi_{-i}}\left[\sum_{t=t^{\prime\prime}}^{t^{\prime}}\gamma^{t}\phi_{t}(s_{t},\boldsymbol{a}_{t})\right]\right| \displaystyle\leq\sum_{t=t^{\prime\prime}}^{t^{\prime}}\gamma^{t}\|\phi\|_{\infty}\leq|\gamma|\frac{\left|\gamma^{t^{\prime\prime}}-\gamma^{t^{\prime}}\right|}{1-\gamma}\|\phi\|_{\infty} \displaystyle\leq|\gamma^{t^{\prime\prime}}|\frac{\left|1-\gamma^{t^{\prime}-t^{\prime\prime}}\right|}{1-\gamma}\|\phi\|_{\infty} \displaystyle\leq\frac{|\gamma^{t^{\prime\prime}}|}{1-\gamma}\|\phi\|_{\infty}=e^{t^{\prime\prime}\ln\gamma}\frac{\|\phi\|_{\infty}}{1-\gamma} \displaystyle=e^{-t^{\prime\prime}|\ln\gamma|}\left(\frac{\|\phi\|_{\infty}}{1-\gamma}\right)\leq e^{-T^{\prime}|\ln\gamma|}\left(\frac{\|\phi\|_{\infty}}{1-\gamma}\right), $$

using Cauchy-Schwarz and since $t^{\prime}\geq t^{\prime\prime}>T^{\prime}$ and $\gamma\in[0,1[$ . The inequality of the proposition is true whenever $T^{\prime}$ is chosen to satisfy

$$ \displaystyle T^{\prime}\geq\left|\ln{(\epsilon)}(\ln{(\gamma)}\left(\frac{\|\phi\|_{\infty}}{1-\gamma}\right)^{-1}\right|, $$

hence the result is proven. ∎

We are now in a position to extend the dynamic potential property (23) to the infinite horizon case:

#### Proof.

The result is proven by contradiction.

To this end, let us firstly assume there exists a constant $c\neq 0$ s.th.

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{s\sim P(\cdot|)}\left[v^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}_{i}(s)-v^{\boldsymbol{\pi^{\prime}}}_{i}(s)\right]-\mathbb{E}_{s\sim P(\cdot|)}\left[B^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}_{i}(s)-B^{\boldsymbol{\pi^{\prime}}}_{i}(s)\right]=c. $$

Let us now define the following quantities for any $s\in\mathcal{S}$ and for each $\pi_{i}\in\Pi_{i}$ and $\pi_{-i}\in\Pi_{-i}$ and $\forall\theta\in\Theta,\forall i\in\mathcal{N}$ :

$$ \displaystyle v_{i,T^{\prime}}^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}(s):=\sum_{t=1}^{T^{\prime}}\int_{\mathcal{S}}ds_{j+1}\mu(s_{0})\pi_{i}(a^{i}_{0},s_{0})\pi_{-i}(a^{-i}_{0},s_{0})\prod_{j=1}^{t-1}\gamma^{j}P(s_{j+1}|s_{j},a^{i}_{j},a^{-i}_{j}) \displaystyle\cdot\pi_{i}(a^{i}_{j}|s_{j})\pi_{-i}(a^{-i}_{j}|s_{j})R_{i}(s_{j},a^{i}_{j},a^{-i}_{j}) $$

and

$$ \displaystyle B_{T^{\prime}}^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}(s) \displaystyle\begin{aligned} :=\sum_{t=1}^{T^{\prime}}\int_{\mathcal{S}}ds_{j+1}\mu(s_{0})\pi_{i}(a^{i}_{0},s_{0})\pi_{-i}(a^{-i}_{0},s_{0})\prod_{j=1}^{t-1}\gamma^{j}P(s_{j+1}|s_{j},a^{i}_{j},a^{-i}_{j})\pi_{i}(a^{i}_{j}|s_{j})\pi_{-i}(a^{-i}_{j}|s_{j})&\\
\cdot\phi(s_{j},a^{i}_{j},a^{-i}_{j})&,\end{aligned} $$

so that the quantity $v_{i,T^{\prime}}^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}(s)$ measures the expected cumulative return until the point $T^{\prime}<\infty$ .

Hence, we straightforwardly deduce that

$$ \displaystyle v_{i}^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}(s)\equiv v_{i,\infty}^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}(s) \displaystyle\begin{aligned} =v_{i,T^{\prime}}^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}(s)+\gamma^{T^{\prime}}\int_{\mathcal{S}}ds_{j+1}\mu(s_{0})\pi_{i}(a^{i}_{0},s_{0})\pi_{-i}(a^{-i}_{0},s_{0})\prod_{j=1}^{T^{\prime}}P(s_{j+1}|s_{j},a^{i}_{j},a^{-i}_{j})\pi_{i}(a^{i}_{j}|s_{j})&\\
\cdot\pi_{-i}(a^{-i}_{j}|s_{j})v_{i}^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}(s_{T^{\prime}}).&\end{aligned} $$

Our first task is to establish that the quantity $\left|\underset{t\to\infty}{\lim}\mathbb{E}_{s\sim P(\cdot|)}\left[B^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}_{i,t}(s)-B^{\boldsymbol{\pi^{\prime}}}_{i,t}(s)\right]\right|$ is in fact, well-defined for any $s\in\mathcal{S}$ and $\forall i\in\mathcal{N}$ .

This is true since by (25) for any $t>0$ we have that

$$ \displaystyle\left|\mathbb{E}_{s\sim P(\cdot|)}\left[B^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}_{i,t}(s)-B^{\boldsymbol{\pi^{\prime}}}_{i,t}(s)\right]\right|=\left|\mathbb{E}_{s\sim P(\cdot|)}\left[v^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}_{i,t}(s)-v^{\boldsymbol{\pi^{\prime}}}_{i,t}(s)\right]\right|, $$

and hence we have that

$$ \displaystyle\left|\mathbb{E}_{s\sim P(\cdot|)}\left[B^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}(s)-B^{\boldsymbol{\pi^{\prime}}}(s)\right]\right|<\infty. $$

To see this, we firstly observe that by the boundedness of $R_{i}$ , $\exists c>0$ s.th. $\forall t\in\mathbb{N},\forall i\in\mathcal{N}$ and for any $\pi_{i}\in\Pi_{i},\pi_{-i}\in\Pi_{-i}$

$$ \displaystyle\left|v^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}_{i,t}(s)-v^{\boldsymbol{\pi^{\prime}}}_{i,t}(s)\right|<c. $$

This is true since for any $k<\infty$ we have

$$ \displaystyle\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad v_{i,k}^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}(s)-v_{i,k}^{\boldsymbol{\pi^{\prime}}}(s) \displaystyle=\mathbb{E}_{s_{t}\sim P,\pi_{i},\pi_{-i}}\left[\sum_{t=0}^{k}\gamma^{t}R_{i}(s_{t},\boldsymbol{a}_{t})\right]-\mathbb{E}_{s_{t}\sim P,\pi^{\prime}_{i},\pi_{-i}}\left[\sum_{t=0}^{k}\gamma^{t}R_{i}(s_{t},\boldsymbol{a}_{t})\right] \displaystyle\leq\left|\mathbb{E}_{s_{t}\sim P,\pi_{i},\pi_{-i}}\left[\sum_{t=0}^{k}\gamma^{t}R_{i}(s_{t},\boldsymbol{a}_{t})\right]-\mathbb{E}_{s_{t}\sim P,\pi^{\prime}_{i},\pi_{-i}}\left[\sum_{t=0}^{k}\gamma^{t}R_{i}(s_{t},\boldsymbol{a}_{t})\right]\right| \displaystyle\leq 2\sum_{t=0}^{k}\gamma^{t}\|R_{i}\|_{\infty}=2\frac{1-\gamma^{k}}{1-\gamma}\|R_{i}\|_{\infty}. $$

Therefore, by the bounded convergence theorem we have that

$$ \displaystyle\underset{t\to\infty}{\lim}\left|\mathbb{E}_{s\sim P(\cdot|)}\left[v^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}_{i,t}(s)-v^{\boldsymbol{\pi^{\prime}}}_{i,t}(s)\right]\right|<\infty. $$

Now, using (29), we deduce that for any $\epsilon>0$ , the following statement holds:

$$ \displaystyle\left|\mathbb{E}_{s\sim P(\cdot|)}\left[B^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}_{i,t}(s)-B^{\boldsymbol{\pi^{\prime}}}_{i,t}(s)\right]\right|<\left|\mathbb{E}_{s\sim P(\cdot|)}\left[v^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}_{i,t}(s)-v^{\boldsymbol{\pi^{\prime}}}_{i,t}(s)\right]\right|+\epsilon, $$

which after taking the limit as $t\to\infty$ and using (30), Lemma D and the dominated convergence theorem, we find that

$$ \displaystyle\underset{t\to\infty}{\lim}\left|\mathbb{E}_{s\sim P(\cdot|)}\left[B^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}_{i,t}(s)-B^{\boldsymbol{\pi^{\prime}}}_{i,t}(s)\right]\right|<\infty. $$

Next we observe that:

$$ \displaystyle c \displaystyle=\mathbb{E}_{s\sim P(\cdot|)}\left[\left(v_{i}^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}-v_{i}^{\boldsymbol{\pi^{\prime}}}\right)(s)\right]-\mathbb{E}_{s\sim P(\cdot|)}\left[\left(B^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}-B^{\boldsymbol{\pi^{\prime}}}\right)(s)\right] \displaystyle=\mathbb{E}_{s\sim P(\cdot|)}\left[\left(v_{i,T^{\prime}}^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}-v_{i,T^{\prime}}^{\boldsymbol{\pi^{\prime}}}\right)(s)\right]-\mathbb{E}_{s\sim P(\cdot|)}\left[\left(B_{T^{\prime}}^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}-B_{T^{\prime}}^{\boldsymbol{\pi^{\prime}}}\right)(s)\right] \displaystyle\begin{aligned} +\gamma^{T^{\prime}}\mathbb{E}_{s_{T^{\prime}}\sim P(\cdot|)}\Bigg[\int_{\mathcal{S}}ds_{j+1}\mu(s_{0})\pi_{i}(a^{i}_{0},s_{0})\pi_{-i}(a^{-i}_{0},s_{0})\prod_{j=1}^{T^{\prime}}P(s_{j+1}|s_{j},a^{i}_{j},a^{-i}_{j})\pi_{i}(a^{i}_{j}|s_{j})\pi_{-i}(a^{-i}_{j}|s_{j})\\
\cdot\left(v_{i}^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}(s_{T^{\prime}})-B^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}(s_{T^{\prime}})\right)&\end{aligned} \displaystyle\begin{aligned} +\int_{\mathcal{S}}ds_{j+1}\mu(s_{0})\pi^{\prime}_{i}(a^{\prime i}_{0},s_{0})\pi_{-i}(a^{-i}_{0},s_{0})\prod_{j=1}^{T^{\prime}}P(s_{j+1}|s_{j},a^{\prime i}_{j},a^{-i}_{j})\pi_{i}(a^{\prime i}_{j}|s_{j})\pi_{-i}(a^{-i}_{j}|s_{j})\\
\cdot\left(v_{i}^{\boldsymbol{\pi^{\prime}}}(s_{T^{\prime}})-B^{\boldsymbol{\pi^{\prime}}}(s_{T^{\prime}})\right)\Bigg].&\end{aligned} $$

Considering the last expectation and its coefficient and denoting it by $\kappa$ , we observe the following bound:

$$ \displaystyle|\kappa|\leq 2\gamma^{T^{\prime}}\left(\|v_{i}\|+\|B\|\right). $$

Since we can choose $T^{\prime}$ freely and $\gamma\in]0,1[$ , we can choose $T^{\prime}$ to be sufficiently large so that

$$ \displaystyle\gamma^{T^{\prime}}\left(\|v_{i}\|+\|B\|\right)<\frac{1}{4}|c|. $$

This then implies that

$$ \displaystyle\left|\mathbb{E}_{s\sim P(\cdot|)}\left[\left(v_{i,T^{\prime}}^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}-v_{i,T^{\prime}}^{\boldsymbol{\pi^{\prime}}}\right)(s)-\left(B_{T^{\prime}}^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}-B_{T^{\prime}}^{\boldsymbol{\pi^{\prime}}}\right)(s)\right]\right|>\frac{1}{2}c, $$

which is a contradiction since we have proven that for any finite $T^{\prime}$ it is the case that

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{s\sim P(\cdot|)}\left[\left(v_{i,T^{\prime}}^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}-v_{i,T^{\prime}}^{\boldsymbol{\pi^{\prime}}}\right)(s)-\left(B_{T^{\prime}}^{\boldsymbol{\pi}}-B_{T^{\prime}}^{\boldsymbol{\pi^{\prime}}}\right)(s)\right]=0, $$

and hence we deduce the thesis. ∎

#### Lemma E.

For any c-SPG the following expression holds $\forall(\boldsymbol{\eta}^{i},\boldsymbol{\eta}^{-i})\in\boldsymbol{E}^{ps},\forall s\in\mathcal{S}$

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{\pi_{i}(\boldsymbol{\eta}_{i}),\pi_{-i}(\boldsymbol{\eta}_{-i})}\left[R_{i}\right]-\mathbb{E}_{\pi_{i}(\boldsymbol{\eta}^{\prime}_{i}),\pi_{-i}(\boldsymbol{\eta}_{-i})}\left[R_{i}\right]=\mathbb{E}_{\pi_{i}(\boldsymbol{\eta}_{i}),\pi_{-i}(\boldsymbol{\eta}_{-i})}\left[\phi\right]-\mathbb{E}_{\pi^{\prime}_{i}(\boldsymbol{\eta}^{\prime}_{i}),\pi_{-i}(\boldsymbol{\eta}_{-i})}\left[\phi\right]. $$

#### Proof of Lemma E.

The forward implication is straightforward.

Indeed, assume that (1) holds, that is:

$$ \displaystyle R_{i}(s_{t},(a^{i}_{t},a^{-i}_{t}))-R_{i}(s_{t},(a^{\prime i}_{t},a^{-i}_{t}))=\phi(s_{t},(a^{i}_{t},a^{-i}_{t}))-\phi(s_{t},(a^{\prime i}_{t},a^{-i}_{t})) $$

Define by $\Delta F[s_{t}](a^{i}_{t},a^{\prime i}_{t}),a^{-i}_{t}):=F(s_{t},(a^{i}_{t},a^{-i}_{t}))-F(s_{t},(a^{\prime i}_{t},a^{-i}_{t}))$ for any $a^{\prime i}_{t}\in\mathcal{A}_{i}$ then for any $F:\mathcal{S}\times\mathcal{A}_{i}\times\mathcal{A}_{-i}\to\mathbb{R}$ ( $F\in\mathcal{H}$ ) we have that

$$ \displaystyle\int_{a_{i}\in\mathcal{A}_{i}}\int_{a^{\prime}_{i}\in\mathcal{A}_{i}}\int_{a_{-i}\in\mathcal{A}_{-i}}\pi_{i}(da^{i}|\cdot)\pi_{i}(da^{\prime i}|\cdot)\pi_{-i}(da^{-i}|\cdot)\Delta F[s_{t}](a^{i}_{t},a^{\prime i}_{t}),a^{-i}_{t}) \displaystyle=\int_{a_{i}\in\mathcal{A}_{i}}\int_{a_{-i}\in\mathcal{A}_{-i}}\pi_{i}(da^{i}|\cdot)\pi_{-i}(da^{-i}|\cdot)F(a^{i}_{t},a^{\prime i}_{t}),a^{-i}_{t})-\int_{a^{\prime}_{i}\in\mathcal{A}_{i}}\int_{a_{-i}\in\mathcal{A}_{-i}}\pi_{i}(da^{\prime i}|\cdot)\pi_{-i}(da^{-i}|\cdot)F(s_{t},(a^{\prime i}_{t},a^{-i}_{t})) \displaystyle=\mathbb{E}_{(\pi_{i},\pi_{-i})}\left[F(s_{t},(a^{i}_{t},a^{-i}_{t}))\right]-\mathbb{E}_{(\pi^{\prime}_{i},\pi_{-i})}\left[F(s_{t},(a^{\prime i}_{t},a^{-i}_{t}))\right] $$

This immediately suggests that we can get the result by multiplying (39) by $\int_{a_{i}\in\mathcal{A}_{i}}\int_{a^{\prime}_{i}\in\mathcal{A}_{i}}\int_{a_{-i}\in\mathcal{A}_{-i}}\pi_{i}(da^{i}|\cdot)\pi_{i}(da^{\prime i}|\cdot)\pi_{-i}(da^{-i}|\cdot)$ .

For the reverse (in pure strategies) we first consider the case in which the pure strategy is a linear map from some parameterisation. We now readily verify that the reverse holds indeed:

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{\pi_{i}(\boldsymbol{\eta}_{i}),\pi_{-i}(\boldsymbol{\eta}_{-i})}\left[F(s,a^{i},a^{-i})\right]-\mathbb{E}_{\pi_{i}(\boldsymbol{\eta}^{\prime}_{i}),\pi_{-i}(\boldsymbol{\eta}_{-i})}\left[F(s,a^{i},a^{-i})\right] \displaystyle=\int_{a^{\prime}\in\mathcal{A}^{i}}\int_{a^{\prime\prime}\in\mathcal{A}^{-i}}\pi_{i}(da^{\prime}|s;\boldsymbol{\eta}_{i})\pi_{-i}(da^{\prime\prime}|s;\boldsymbol{\eta}_{-i})F_{i}(s,(a^{\prime},a^{\prime\prime})) \displaystyle\qquad-\int_{a^{\prime}\in\mathcal{A}^{i}}\int_{a^{\prime\prime}\in\mathcal{A}^{-i}}\pi_{i}(da^{\prime}|s;\boldsymbol{\eta}^{\prime}_{i})\pi_{-i}(da^{\prime\prime}|s;\boldsymbol{\eta}_{-i})F_{i}(s,(a^{\prime},a^{\prime\prime})) \displaystyle=\int_{a^{\prime}\in\mathcal{A}^{i}}\int_{a^{\prime\prime}\in\mathcal{A}^{-i}}da^{\prime}da^{\prime\prime}\delta_{i}(a^{\prime}-a^{i}(s;\boldsymbol{\eta}_{i}))\delta_{-i}(a^{\prime\prime}-a^{-i}(s;\boldsymbol{\eta}_{-i}))F_{i}(s,(a^{\prime},a^{\prime\prime})) \displaystyle\qquad-\int_{a^{\prime}\in\mathcal{A}^{i}}\int_{a^{\prime\prime}\in\mathcal{A}^{-i}}da^{\prime}da^{\prime\prime}\delta_{i}(a^{\prime}-a^{i}(s;\boldsymbol{\eta}^{\prime}_{i}))\delta_{-i}(a^{\prime\prime}-a^{-i}(s;\boldsymbol{\eta}_{-i}))F_{i}(s,(a^{\prime},a^{\prime\prime})) \displaystyle=\Delta F_{i}(s,(a^{i}(s;\boldsymbol{\eta}_{i}),a^{-i}(s;\boldsymbol{\eta}_{-i}))) $$

which proves the statement in the linear case.

For the general case, consider a strategy which is defined by a map $h:\mathcal{S}\times E\to\mathcal{A}$ . We note that for any $\beta\in\mathbb{R}/\{0\}$ and $x\in X\subset\mathbb{R}$ we have that

$$ \displaystyle\int_{\mathbb{R}}\delta(\beta x)=\frac{1}{|\beta|}\int_{\mathbb{R}}\delta(\beta x)dx $$

This is true since for any $\beta\in\mathbb{R}/\{0\}$ we can construct the delta function in the following way:

$$ \displaystyle\delta(\beta x)=\underset{m\to\infty}{\lim}\frac{1}{|m|\sqrt{\pi}}e^{-\left(\beta x/m\right)^{2}} $$

Now define $n:=m\beta^{-1}$ , then

$$ \displaystyle\underset{m\to\infty}{\lim}\frac{1}{|m|\sqrt{\pi}}e^{-\left(\beta x/m\right)^{2}} \displaystyle=\underset{n\to\infty}{\lim}\frac{1}{|\beta n|\sqrt{\pi}}e^{-\left(x/n\right)^{2}} \displaystyle=\frac{1}{|\beta|}\underset{n\to\infty}{\lim}\frac{1}{|n|\sqrt{\pi}}e^{-\left(x/n\right)^{2}}=\frac{1}{|\beta|}\delta(x) $$

In the following, we use the coarea formula (for geometric measures) (Simon et al., 1983; Nicolaescu, 2011) which says that for any open set $X\subset\mathbb{R}^{n}$ and for any Lipschitz function $f:X\to\mathbb{R}$ on $X$ and for any $L^{1}$ function $g$ the following expression holds:

$$ \displaystyle\int_{X}g(x)|\nabla f(x)|dx=\int_{\mathbb{R}}\left(\int_{f^{-1}(s)}g(x)dH_{n-1}(x)\right)ds $$

where $H_{n-1}$ is the $(n-1)-$ dimensional Hausdorff measure.

Let us now define $k(s,\boldsymbol{\eta},a):=h^{-1}(s,\boldsymbol{\eta})-a$ .

Now

$$ \displaystyle\int_{a\in\mathcal{A}}\pi_{\epsilon=0}(a;s,\boldsymbol{\eta})F_{i}(s,\boldsymbol{a})da=\int_{a\in\mathcal{A}}\delta(k(s,a,h(\boldsymbol{\eta})))F_{i}(s,\boldsymbol{a})da $$

By Taylor’s theorem, expanding about the point $y$ where $y$ is defined by $k(s,\boldsymbol{\eta},y)=0$ implies that

$$ \displaystyle\int_{a\in\mathcal{A}}\delta(k(s,a,\boldsymbol{\eta}))F_{i}(s,\boldsymbol{a})da\approx\int_{a\in\mathcal{A}}\delta\left(k^{\prime}(s,y,\boldsymbol{\eta})(a-y)\right)F_{i}(s,\boldsymbol{a})da $$

Moreover

$$ \displaystyle\int_{a\in\mathcal{A}}\delta(k^{\prime}(s,y,\boldsymbol{\eta}))(a-y)F_{i}(s,\boldsymbol{a})da \displaystyle=\int_{y\in k^{-1}(0)}\left(\int^{y+\epsilon}_{y-\epsilon}\delta\left(k^{\prime}(s,y,\boldsymbol{\eta})(a-y)\right)F_{i}(s,\boldsymbol{a})da\right)d\sigma(y) $$

where $\sigma$ is a Minkowski content measure.

Define $x:=a-y$ so $dx:=da$

$$ \displaystyle\int_{y\in k^{-1}(0)}\left(\int^{y+\epsilon}_{y-\epsilon}\delta\left(k^{\prime}(s,y,g(\boldsymbol{\eta}))(a-y)\right)F_{i}(s,\boldsymbol{a})da\right)d\sigma(y) \displaystyle=\int_{y\in k^{-1}(0)}\left(\int^{x+\epsilon}_{x-\epsilon}\delta\left(k^{\prime}(s,y,\boldsymbol{\eta})x\right)F_{i}(s,x+y)dx\right)d\sigma(y) \displaystyle=\int_{y\in k^{-1}(0)}\left(\int^{x+\epsilon}_{x-\epsilon}\delta(x)\frac{F(s,x+y)}{|k^{\prime}(s,y,\boldsymbol{\eta})|}dx\right)d\sigma(y) \displaystyle=\int_{y\in k^{-1}(0)}\frac{F_{i}(s,y)}{|k^{\prime}(s,y,\boldsymbol{\eta})|}d\sigma(y) \displaystyle=\int_{y\in k^{-1}(0)}F_{i}(s,y)d\sigma(y) \displaystyle=F_{i}(s,a) $$

#### Proof of Prop. 3.

We first show that the Bellman operator is a contraction. Indeed, for any bounded $F,F^{\prime}\in\mathcal{H}$ we have

$$ \displaystyle\left\|\left[T_{\phi}F\right]-\left[T_{\phi}F^{\prime}\right]\right\|\leq\gamma d $$

where $d:=\|F-F^{\prime}\|_{\infty}$ using the fact that $T_{\phi}$ is monotonic.

$$ \displaystyle\left\|\left[T^{k}_{\phi}F\right]-\left[T^{k}_{\phi_{\epsilon}}F^{\prime}\right]\right\| \displaystyle\leq\left\|\phi-\phi_{\epsilon}\right\|_{\infty}+\gamma\left\|T^{k-1}_{\phi}F-T^{k-1}_{\phi_{\epsilon}}F^{\prime}\right\|_{\infty} \displaystyle\leq\epsilon+\sum_{j=0}^{m-1}\gamma^{j}\left\|\phi-\phi_{\epsilon}\right\|_{\infty}+\gamma^{m}\left\|T^{k-m}_{\phi}F-T^{k-m}_{\phi_{\epsilon}}F^{\prime}\right\|_{\infty} \displaystyle\leq\epsilon+\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}\gamma^{j}\left\|\phi-\phi_{\epsilon}\right\|_{\infty}+\gamma^{k}d \displaystyle\leq\epsilon\left(1+\frac{1-\gamma^{k}}{1-\gamma}\right)+\gamma^{k}d $$
